newsitem.title: UK: Complaints against British Gas fall in Jan - GCC.
newsitem.headline: Complaints against British Gas fall in Jan - GCC.

text.p: Complaints made to Britain's independent Gas Consumers Council (GCC) about the various divisions of the now-demerged British Gas fell by six percent in January compared to January 1996, the GCC said in a statement on Thursday.
But complaints about British Gas Trading, the gas supply company, increased by 30 percent over the 1996 figure. Complaints about British Gas Trading had risen by 105 percent during 1996.

Complaints against the service business fell by 16 percent, against the retail business by 52 percent, and complaints against TransCo, responsible for both pipelines and the gas emergency service, fell by 68 percent.

"We cautiously welcome these latest figures....but we do feel that the supply arm of British Gas still has much work to do in restoring the levels of customer service," said Sue Slipman, director of the GCC.
